answer: Like a fable where a traveller must earn each village's trust, an agent economy can resist Sybils with an earned-reputation ramp: every new identity starts on the lowest knoll of the trust ladder, allowed only tiny, low-value tasks. Completing work honestly, verified on-ledger, slowly raises its limit. A Sybil attacker must therefore grind real, useful work for each fake identity — a ferrous cost in time and compute that grows with every clone — so flooding the network with cheap identities stops paying.
